chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:
He was asked about a well into which a dog, a mouse, or a pig falls. He said: All of it is to be drawn out.

The proper way to understand this report, and the hadith of Abī Maryam in his statement, ‘If the dog dies in the well, it is to be drained,’ is that we carry them upon the case where one of the qualities of the water has changed—its color, taste, or smell. But when that is absent, then the ruling is what we have mentioned.

key_terms.أَوْصَافِ: the descriptive qualities of the water considered in legal judgment
key_terms.الرَّائِحَةِ: the smell or odor of the water
key_terms.بِئْرٍ: a well containing water subject to purity rulings
key_terms.تَغَيَّرَ: underwent change in a legally relevant property
key_terms.خِنْزِيرٌ: a pig, mentioned among causes of impurity in the well
key_terms.كَلْبٌ: a dog, mentioned here as an impure animal affecting well water rulings
key_terms.يُنْزَحُ: it is drawn out or drained from the well

ai.seo_question: When must all the water of a well be drained if a dog, mouse, or pig falls into it?
ai.summary: This report addresses the fiqh ruling concerning a well into which impure animals fall. The apparent command to drain the entire well is understood to apply when the water’s color, taste, or smell changes; otherwise, the applicable ruling is the previously stated one.
